<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

## Objective
- Overhaul the survival game in `index.html`, preserving established layout and gameplay while addressing roadside skill-option duplication and distance-based vehicle part rarity and stats.

## Requirements
- Preserve layout, resource/action placement, journey and road-log placement, Van Rig position, resource tiers, repair supplies, part rarity colors, and crew-stress behavior.
- Keep Hull visible in the market; crew skills have two charges per run, camping does not restore charges, and each crew member can recharge once per market for 10 Scrap.
- Keep full skill descriptions on crew cards and concise labels on event skill choices.
- Standard roadside events should have 3–4 contextual choices; avoid generic Ammo trades and universal skill bypasses.
- Use high-cost Ammo trades only in a rare standalone roadside encounter; show skill bypasses only when a trait logically fits.
- Event helper text and numeric keyboard controls should reflect available choices; choices past ten use letter shortcuts.
- Unify applicable crew-trait roadside options so a trait does not appear as both a free-action and a charge-consuming option on one card.
- Set vehicle part/tire rarity odds by odometer: Rusted common before 200 miles, then phases out; Worn uncommon before 200, common after; Normal rare before 200, uncommon after 200, common after 300; Pristine very rare before 200, rare after 200, uncommon after 350.
- Balance stats by tier: Pristine has very high bonus or 2–3 strong medium bonuses with few drawbacks; Normal is roughly ¾ Pristine with 1–2 medium/high bonuses and 0–2 minor drawbacks; Worn is roughly ½ maximum Pristine with low/medium bonuses and 1–2 clear drawbacks; Rusted has low baseline bonuses above starting gear and at least one mandatory drawback.

## Decisions
- Roadside skill choices are event-specific; Sharpshooter applies only to hostile hazards, while Tinkerer bypasses Scrap Storm.
- Skill bypass consumes one charge and clears pending crew-event effects.
- Ammo trader is a standalone encounter selected at 7% chance, without a random crew update.
- Market recharge allowance is tracked per crew member per market stop.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing `index.html` changes implement market Hull visibility, two charges per run, camp helper text, per-member 10-Scrap market recharge, skill descriptions, contextual roadside choices and bypasses, standalone Ammo trader, and choice-specific helper/keyboard shortcuts.
- Current inline JavaScript passed `node --check`; `git diff --check` passed during review.

### Active
- Implement the newly requested unified trait option behavior and odometer-based part/tire rarity odds and tier stat balancing in `index.html`.
- Previous work is uncommitted in `index.html`.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect current `index.html` part/tire generation and event special/skill option code.
2. Implement unified contextual trait options and the requested rarity milestone distributions and tier-specific stat balance.
3. Validate inline JavaScript syntax, whitespace, and gameplay behavior; review the final diff.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, event pool and choice handling, market generation, vehicle parts/tires, and resource handling.

## Important Context
- Current roadside events use `specials` plus `eventSkillOptions()`; the current arrangement may show duplicate trait options and needs consolidation.
- `showMarket()` generates `marketStock` through `makeMarketPart(part,dist,index)`; rarity/stat logic should be traced there and in the related catalog/generation helpers.
- Git status previously showed only `M index.html`; the work is uncommitted.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Overhaul the survival game in `index.html`, preserving its established layout and gameplay while fixing duplicate roadside trait options and overhauling distance-based vehicle-part rarity and stats.

## Requirements
- Preserve layout, resource/action placement, journey and road-log placement, Van Rig position, resource tiers, repair supplies, part rarity colors, and crew-stress behavior.
- Keep Hull visible in the market; crew skills have two charges per run, camping does not restore charges, and each crew member can recharge once per market for 10 Scrap.
- Keep full skill descriptions on crew cards and concise labels on event skill choices.
- Standard roadside events should have 3–4 contextual choices; avoid generic Ammo trades and universal skill bypasses.
- Use high-cost Ammo trades only in a rare standalone roadside encounter; show skill bypasses only when a trait logically fits.
- Event helper text and numeric keyboard controls should reflect available choices; choices past ten use letter shortcuts.
- Unify applicable crew-trait roadside options so a trait does not appear as both a free-action and a charge-consuming option on one card.
- Part/tire rarity by odometer: Rusted common before 200 miles, then phases out; Worn uncommon before 200, common after; Normal rare before 200, uncommon after 200, common after 300; Pristine very rare before 200, rare after 200, uncommon after 350.
- Balance tiers: Pristine has very high bonuses or 2–3 strong medium bonuses with few drawbacks; Normal roughly ¾ Pristine with 1–2 medium-to-high bonuses and 0–2 minor drawbacks; Worn roughly ½ maximum Pristine with low/medium bonuses and 1–2 clear drawbacks; Rusted low baseline bonuses above starting gear and at least one mandatory drawback.

## Decisions
- Roadside skill choices are event-specific; Sharpshooter applies only to hostile hazards, while Tinkerer bypasses Scrap Storm.
- Skill bypass consumes one charge and clears pending crew-event effects.
- Ammo trader is a standalone encounter selected at 7% chance, without a random crew update.
- Market recharge allowance is tracked per crew member per market stop.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing `index.html` changes implement Hull visibility in the market, two charges per run, camp helper text, per-member 10-Scrap market recharge, skill descriptions, contextual roadside choices and bypasses, standalone Ammo trader, and choice-specific helper/keyboard shortcuts.
- Inline JavaScript syntax and `git diff --check` previously passed.

### Active
- Fix duplicate trait options and implement odometer-based rarity distributions and tier-specific stat balancing in `index.html`.
- Current part generation has three tiers and assigns Rusted and Worn to the first two market slots regardless of distance; `makeMarketPart` scales base stats and drawbacks together.
- Roadside rendering independently appends one matching `specials` option and all eligible `eventSkillOptions()`, which can duplicate a trait.

### Blocked
- An attempted replacement of `conditionTiers`, `conditionForDistance`, and `makeMarketPart` failed because the exact source text did not match; no changes from that attempt were applied.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and replace the existing part-tier generation block in `index.html` using its exact current source.
2. Update market rarity helper text to accurately describe the new tiers and milestone odds.
3. Consolidate applicable trait options during roadside event construction so a trait appears only once per card.
4. Validate inline JavaScript syntax, run `git diff --check`, and review the final diff.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, roadside event choices and skill handling, market generation, and vehicle part/tire data.

## Important Context
- Current part catalog has nine bases, each with a primary stat and a downside; starter gear is negative or detrimental in each corresponding slot.
- Current part tiers are Rusted/Worn/Pristine only, and the market assigns Rusted to slot 0 and Worn to slot 1 regardless of distance.
- `showEvent()` constructs choices from `ev.choices`, one matching `ev.specials` entry, and `eventSkillOptions()`.
- Changes in `index.html` are uncommitted.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Overhaul the survival game in `index.html` while preserving established layout and gameplay.
- Add minor roadside salvage discoveries and rebalance the rare ammo-broker encounter.

## Requirements
- Preserve layout, resource/action placement, journey and road-log placement, Van Rig position, resource tiers, repair supplies, part rarity colors, and crew-stress behavior.
- Keep Hull visible in the market; crew skills have two charges per run, camping does not restore charges, and each crew member can recharge once per market for 10 Scrap.
- Keep full skill descriptions on crew cards and concise labels on event skill choices.
- Standard roadside events should have 3–4 contextual choices; avoid generic Ammo trades and universal skill bypasses.
- Use high-cost Ammo trades only in a rare standalone roadside encounter; show skill bypasses only when a trait logically fits.
- Event helper text and numeric keyboard controls should reflect available choices; choices past ten use letter shortcuts.
- Unify applicable crew-trait roadside options so a trait does not appear as both a free-action and a charge-consuming option on one card.
- Part/tire rarity by odometer: Rusted common before 200 miles, then phases out; Worn uncommon before 200, common after; Normal rare before 200, uncommon after 200, common after 300; Pristine very rare before 200, rare after 200, uncommon after 350.
- Balance tiers: Pristine has very high bonuses or 2–3 strong medium bonuses with few drawbacks; Normal roughly ¾ Pristine with 1–2 medium-to-high bonuses and 0–2 minor drawbacks; Worn roughly ½ maximum Pristine with low/medium bonuses and 1–2 clear drawbacks; Rusted low baseline bonuses above starting gear and at least one mandatory drawback.
- Minor road salvage should occur roughly every 25–40 miles between major events, add a short character-driven discovery line attributed to a living crew member, and grant +2–6 Scrap, +1–2 Fuel, or a rare ammo find.
- Ammo broker exact options: [1] 25 Rations for +1 ammo, stress MV +10, ET +10, JP +5; [2] 30 Fuel for +1 ammo, stress MV +15, ET +5, JP -5; [3] 30 Scrap for +1 ammo, stress MV -5, ET -5, JP -5; [4] refuse with no resource or stress change.
- Add clean spacing or a visual badge separator between the ammo option text and the `INSUFFICIENT RESOURCES` warning.

## Decisions
- Roadside skill choices are event-specific; Sharpshooter applies only to hostile hazards, while Tinkerer bypasses Scrap Storm.
- Skill bypass consumes one charge and clears pending crew-event effects.
- Ammo trader is a standalone encounter selected at 7% chance, without a random crew update.
- Market recharge allowance is tracked per crew member per market stop.
- Part odds use distance-based weight bands with interpolation between 200, 300, and 350 miles; tier stats and drawbacks scale separately.
- Minor salvage awards use the existing Scrap multiplier and respect Fuel’s 100-unit cap.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` contains the market, crew-skill, roadside-event, Ammo trader, helper-text, and keyboard-control changes.
- Added Rusted/Worn/Normal/Pristine part tiers, distance-based generation and rarity labels, tier-specific stat/drawback scaling, and updated market odds text and Normal-tier styling.
- Filtered roadside skill choices to avoid duplicating a trait already offered as a special event choice.
- Added randomized minor salvage at 25–40 mile intervals, with living-crew attribution and Scrap, Fuel, or rare ammo rewards.
- Inline JavaScript syntax check and `git diff --check` passed after salvage implementation.
- Changes are uncommitted; prior status showed only `index.html` modified.

### Active
- Rebalance `ammoTradeEvent` costs and implement its specified per-member stress effects.
- Fix spacing/separator for the insufficient-resources warning in event choices.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Update `ammoTradeEvent` options in `index.html` to exact costs and text.
2. Apply the specified MV/ET/JP stress changes only when one of the first three broker trades is chosen; refusal must change neither resources nor stress.
3. Add spacing or a badge separator before the insufficient-resource warning and verify the resulting event choice markup.
4. Run inline JavaScript syntax validation and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, road events and logs, broker choices, stress handling, market generation, and vehicle-part/tire data.

## Important Context
- Part generation uses Rusted/Worn/Normal/Pristine power factors `.3/.6/.9/1.2` and drawback factors `1.5/1/.35/.1`.
- Distance weights are `[56,30,12,2]` before 200 miles, interpolate toward `[18,42,32,8]` at 200 and `[0,40,43,17]` at 300, then `[0,35,45,20]` at 350; Rusted rarity text becomes Uncommon after 200 even as its weight phases out.
- Broker definition is at line 223; generic choice effects and affordability markup are in `choose(c)` and `showEvent()` near lines 269–271.

"Overhaul the Camp System with persistent Camp Threat, Camp Exhaustion, and tiered disturbance events:
1. Camp State & 50-Mile Cooldown: Track campThreat, campExhaustion, and milesSinceCampReset. Both campThreat and campExhaustion increase with each camp scavenging action and persist if the player leaves camp early—they only reset after driving 50 miles down the highway.
2. Threat Tiers & Atmospheric Warnings: Progression scales across four visible tiers based on camp actions:   QUIET (Actions 1–2): Low danger, normal resource returns.   UNSETTLED (Actions 3–4): Append atmospheric road-log warnings about distant motorcycle engines and headlights on the horizon; trigger minor disturbances.   EXPOSED (Actions 5–6): Escalate road-log tension (engines idling nearby, campfire smoke spotted); disturbances carry larger resource costs and possible Hull/Vitals damage.   COMPROMISED (Actions 7+): Urgent warnings of approaching figures and sweeping headlights; severe resource losses or forced evacuation. Never trigger scripted motorcycle raid combat or consume Blaster Ammo automatically during camp events.
3. Diminishing Returns & Camp Economy: Scale Scrap yields so a short stay (1–2 actions) nets ~10–25 Scrap, a moderate stay (3–4 actions) nets ~30–50 Scrap, and an extended stay (5+ actions) nets ~60–90 gross Scrap with heavy diminishing returns from campExhaustion. Retain small 1–3 Ration and 4–6 Fuel discoveries.
4. Threat-Scaled Camp Events: Scale disturbance resource costs and stress penalties dynamically by current campThreat tier (Unsettled / Exposed / Compromised), and add the 'Night Watch / Headlights on the Ridge' event featuring choices to wait them out (-Rations, +Stress), barricade (-Scrap), flee (-Fuel, ends camp), [Paranoid] conceal campsite (-4 Scrap, reduces Paranoid crew stress), and [Sharpshooter] watch the ridge (costs 1 charge, no material cost)."

## Objective
- Overhaul the survival game in `index.html` while preserving established layout and gameplay.
- Rebalance the rare ammo-broker encounter’s trade costs and crew stress impacts, and improve insufficient-resource warning spacing.

## Requirements
- Preserve layout, resource/action placement, journey and road-log placement, Van Rig position, resource tiers, repair supplies, part rarity colors, and crew-stress behavior.
- Keep Hull visible in the market; crew skills have two charges per run, camping does not restore charges, and each crew member can recharge once per market for 10 Scrap.
- Keep full skill descriptions on crew cards and concise labels on event skill choices.
- Standard roadside events should have 3–4 contextual choices; avoid generic Ammo trades and universal skill bypasses.
- Use high-cost Ammo trades only in a rare standalone roadside encounter; show skill bypasses only when a trait logically fits.
- Event helper text and numeric keyboard controls should reflect available choices; choices past ten use letter shortcuts.
- Unify applicable crew-trait roadside options so a trait does not appear as both a free-action and a charge-consuming option on one card.
- Part/tire rarity by odometer: Rusted common before 200 miles, then phases out; Worn uncommon before 200, common after; Normal rare before 200, uncommon after 200, common after 300; Pristine very rare before 200, rare after 200, uncommon after 350.
- Balance tiers: Pristine has very high bonuses or 2–3 strong medium bonuses with few drawbacks; Normal roughly ¾ Pristine with 1–2 medium-to-high bonuses and 0–2 minor drawbacks; Worn roughly ½ maximum Pristine with low/medium bonuses and 1–2 clear drawbacks; Rusted low baseline bonuses above starting gear and at least one mandatory drawback.
- Minor roadside salvage should occur roughly every 25–40 miles between major events, add a short character-driven discovery line attributed to a living crew member, and grant +2–6 Scrap, +1–2 Fuel, or a rare ammo find.
- Ammo broker exact options: [1] 25 Rations for +1 ammo, stress MV +10, ET +10, JP +5; [2] 30 Fuel for +1 ammo, stress MV +15, ET +5, JP -5; [3] 30 Scrap for +1 ammo, stress MV -5, ET -5, JP -5; [4] refuse with no resource or stress change.
- Add clean spacing or a visual badge separator between ammo option text and the `INSUFFICIENT RESOURCES` warning.

## Decisions
- Roadside skill choices are event-specific; Sharpshooter applies only to hostile hazards, while Tinkerer bypasses Scrap Storm.
- Skill bypass consumes one charge and clears pending crew-event effects.
- Ammo trader is a standalone encounter selected at 7% chance, without a random crew update.
- Market recharge allowance is tracked per crew member per market stop.
- Part odds use distance-based weight bands with interpolation between 200, 300, and 350 miles; tier stats and drawbacks scale separately.
- Minor salvage awards use the existing Scrap multiplier and respect Fuel’s 100-unit cap.
- Broker stress is applied per member by initials; generic disposition-based stress does not additionally affect broker choices.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` contains the market, crew-skill, roadside-event, broker encounter selection, helper-text, and keyboard-control changes.
- Added Rusted/Worn/Normal/Pristine part tiers, distance-based generation and rarity labels, tier-specific stat/drawback scaling, and updated market odds text and Normal-tier styling.
- Filtered roadside skill choices to avoid duplicating a trait already offered as a special event choice.
- Added randomized minor salvage at 25–40 mile intervals, with living-crew attribution and Scrap, Fuel, or rare ammo rewards.
- Updated broker costs and per-member stress; refusal changes no resources or stress, and broker resolution skips generic disposition stress.
- Inline JavaScript syntax validation (`node --check`) and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Add spacing or a visual badge separator before the `INSUFFICIENT RESOURCES` warning in event choices.
- Review the full final diff, including the dense event-choice HTML template.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the complete event-choice HTML template in `showEvent()` and style the insufficient-resource warning with spacing or a separator.
2. Run inline JavaScript syntax validation and `git diff --check` again; review the final diff.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, broker choices and resolution, roadside events, market, part generation, and salvage.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Broker options store stress in a `stress` map keyed by `MV`, `ET`, and `JP`; refusal has no stress property.
- `applyStress(member, amount)` clamps stress and may trigger a meltdown at 100.
- The broker resolver now checks `currentRoadEvent===ammoTradeEvent` and applies broker stress only to living members; refusal skips both broker-specific and generic disposition stress.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Overhaul the survival game in `index.html` while preserving its established layout and gameplay. Finish camp-system balancing and validate the changes.

## Requirements
- Preserve layout, resource/action placement, journey and road-log placement, Van Rig position, resource tiers, repair supplies, part rarity colors, and crew-stress behavior.
- Keep Hull visible in the market; crew skills have two charges per run, camping does not restore charges, and each crew member can recharge once per market for 10 Scrap.
- Keep full skill descriptions on crew cards and concise labels on event skill choices.
- Standard roadside events should have 3–4 contextual choices; avoid generic Ammo trades and universal skill bypasses.
- Use high-cost Ammo trades only in a rare standalone roadside encounter; show skill bypasses only when a trait logically fits.
- Event helper text and numeric keyboard controls should reflect available choices; choices past ten use letter shortcuts.
- Unify applicable crew-trait roadside options so a trait does not appear as both a free-action and a charge-consuming option on one card.
- Part/tire rarity by odometer: Rusted common before 200 miles, then phases out; Worn uncommon before 200, common after; Normal rare before 200, uncommon after 200, common after 300; Pristine very rare before 200, rare after 200, uncommon after 350.
- Balance part tiers from Pristine through Rusted, with tier-appropriate bonuses and drawbacks.
- Minor roadside salvage should occur roughly every 25–40 miles between major events, with a living crew member’s discovery line and Scrap, Fuel, or rare Ammo.
- Ammo broker exact trades: 25 Rations for +1 Ammo (MV +10 stress, ET +10, JP +5); 30 Fuel for +1 Ammo (MV +15, ET +5, JP -5); 30 Scrap for +1 Ammo (MV -5, ET -5, JP -5); refusal has no resource or stress change.
- Add spacing or a separator before the `INSUFFICIENT RESOURCES` warning in event choices.
- Camp state: `campThreat`, `campExhaustion`, and `milesSinceCampReset`; camp actions increase threat/exhaustion, which persist when leaving camp and reset only after driving 50 miles.
- Camp threat tiers: QUIET (actions 1–2), UNSETTLED (3–4), EXPOSED (5–6), COMPROMISED (7+), with tier-appropriate warnings and escalating disturbances, resource costs, and possible Hull/Vitals damage.
- Camp events must never trigger motorcycle raid combat or automatically consume Blaster Ammo.
- Camp Scrap yields should target ~10–25 for short stays, ~30–50 moderate, ~60–90 gross extended stays, with heavy exhaustion-based diminishing returns; retain small Ration/Fuel finds.
- Add “Night Watch / Headlights on the Ridge” choices: wait (-Rations, +Stress), barricade (-Scrap), flee (-Fuel, ends camp), Paranoid concealment (-4 Scrap and reduces Paranoid stress), Sharpshooter watch (1 charge, no material cost).

## Decisions
- Roadside skill choices are event-specific; Sharpshooter applies only to hostile hazards, while Tinkerer bypasses Scrap Storm.
- Skill bypass consumes one charge and clears pending crew-event effects.
- Ammo trader is a standalone encounter selected at 7% chance, without a random crew update.
- Market recharge allowance is tracked per crew member per market stop.
- Part odds use distance-based weight bands with interpolation at 200, 300, and 350 miles; tier stats and drawbacks scale separately.
- Minor salvage awards use the existing Scrap multiplier and respect Fuel’s 100-unit cap.
- Broker stress is applied per member by initials; generic disposition-based stress does not additionally apply to broker choices.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing `index.html` contains the market, crew-skill, roadside-event, broker encounter, part-tier generation, and minor-salvage updates.
- Broker costs, member-specific stress, and refusal behavior are implemented.
- Added camp-state variables `campThreat`, `campExhaustion`, `milesSinceCampReset`, `campActions`, and `campResetMiles` beside existing camp declarations.

### Active
- Implement persistent camp threat/exhaustion and 50-mile reset behavior.
- Replace generic camp disturbance with tiered warnings and Night Watch choices, preserving separation from raid combat and Ammo.
- Scale camp Scrap yields by actions and exhaustion.
- Add spacing/separator styling for `INSUFFICIENT RESOURCES`.
- Review final diff and rerun syntax and whitespace validation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Update camp resource discovery and disturbance logic in `index.html` to use the new state variables and requested tiered choices.
2. Update driving-distance handling in `tick()` for the 50-mile camp-state reset and tier warnings.
3. Add spacing or a separator before `INSUFFICIENT RESOURCES`.
4. Run inline JavaScript syntax validation and `git diff --check`, then review the final diff.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI and all game logic; current changes are uncommitted.

## Important Context
- Camp logic is around lines 258–263: `showCampNoise()`, `resolveCampNoise()`, `findCampResources()`, `updateCamp()`, and `toggleCamp()`.
- Existing disturbance uses `campNoiseCount`; resource discovery currently yields 6–29 Scrap before multipliers.
- Driving distance advances in `tick()` around line 337; camp threat must not trigger or alter `showRaid()`.
- Recent work only added camp state declarations; no camp behavior or styling has yet been changed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Overhaul the survival game in `index.html` while preserving its established layout and gameplay. Finish camp-system balancing and validate the changes.

## Requirements
- Preserve layout, resource/action placement, journey and road-log placement, Van Rig position, resource tiers, repair supplies, part rarity colors, and crew-stress behavior.
- Keep Hull visible in the market; crew skills have two charges per run, camping does not restore charges, and each crew member can recharge once per market for 10 Scrap.
- Keep full skill descriptions on crew cards and concise labels on event skill choices.
- Standard roadside events should have 3–4 contextual choices; avoid generic Ammo trades and universal skill bypasses.
- Use high-cost Ammo trades only in a rare standalone roadside encounter; show skill bypasses only when a trait logically fits.
- Event helper text and numeric keyboard controls should reflect available choices; choices past ten use letter shortcuts.
- Unify applicable crew-trait roadside options so a trait does not appear as both a free-action and a charge-consuming option on one card.
- Part/tire rarity by odometer: Rusted common before 200 miles, then phases out; Worn uncommon before 200, common after; Normal rare before 200, uncommon after 200, common after 300; Pristine very rare before 200, rare after 200, uncommon after 350.
- Balance part tiers from Pristine through Rusted, with tier-appropriate bonuses and drawbacks.
- Minor roadside salvage should occur roughly every 25–40 miles between major events, with a living crew member’s discovery line and Scrap, Fuel, or rare Ammo.
- Ammo broker exact trades: 25 Rations for +1 Ammo (MV +10 stress, ET +10, JP +5); 30 Fuel for +1 Ammo (MV +15, ET +5, JP -5); 30 Scrap for +1 Ammo (MV -5, ET -5, JP -5); refusal has no resource or stress change.
- Add spacing or a separator before the `INSUFFICIENT RESOURCES` warning in event choices.
- Camp state: `campThreat`, `campExhaustion`, and `milesSinceCampReset`; camp actions increase threat/exhaustion, which persist when leaving camp and reset only after driving 50 miles.
- Camp threat tiers: QUIET (actions 1–2), UNSETTLED (3–4), EXPOSED (5–6), COMPROMISED (7+), with tier-appropriate warnings and escalating disturbances, resource costs, and possible Hull/Vitals damage.
- Camp events must never trigger motorcycle raid combat or automatically consume Blaster Ammo.
- Camp Scrap yields should target ~10–25 for short stays, ~30–50 moderate, ~60–90 gross extended stays, with heavy exhaustion-based diminishing returns; retain small Ration/Fuel finds.
- Add “Night Watch / Headlights on the Ridge” choices: wait (-Rations, +Stress), barricade (-Scrap), flee (-Fuel, ends camp), Paranoid concealment (-4 Scrap and reduces Paranoid stress), Sharpshooter watch (1 charge, no material cost).

## Decisions
- Roadside skill choices are event-specific; Sharpshooter applies only to hostile hazards, while Tinkerer bypasses Scrap Storm.
- Skill bypass consumes one charge and clears pending crew-event effects.
- Ammo trader is a standalone encounter selected at 7% chance, without a random crew update.
- Market recharge allowance is tracked per crew member per market stop.
- Part odds use distance-based weight bands with interpolation at 200, 300, and 350 miles; tier stats and drawbacks scale separately.
- Minor salvage awards use the existing Scrap multiplier and respect Fuel’s 100-unit cap.
- Broker stress is applied per member by initials; generic disposition-based stress does not additionally apply to broker choices.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing `index.html` contains the market, crew-skill, roadside-event, broker encounter, part-tier generation, and minor-salvage updates.
- Broker costs, member-specific stress, and refusal behavior are implemented.
- Added camp-state variables `campThreat`, `campExhaustion`, `milesSinceCampReset`, `campActions`, and `campResetMiles` beside existing camp declarations.

### Active
- Implement persistent camp threat/exhaustion and 50-mile reset behavior.
- Replace generic camp disturbance with tiered warnings and Night Watch choices, preserving separation from raid combat and Ammo.
- Scale camp Scrap yields by actions and exhaustion.
- Add spacing or a separator before `INSUFFICIENT RESOURCES`.
- Review final diff and rerun syntax and whitespace validation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Replace `showCampNoise()`, `resolveCampNoise()`, and `findCampResources()` in `index.html` using exact function boundaries; previous scripted replacement failed because its expected boundary text did not match.
2. Update `tick()` to track driving miles since camp reset and reset threat/exhaustion only after 50 miles.
3. Add warning spacing/separator styling for `INSUFFICIENT RESOURCES`.
4. Run inline JavaScript syntax validation and `git diff --check`, then review the final diff.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, camp logic, and all game behavior; current changes are uncommitted.

## Important Context
- Working tree shows `index.html` modified; earlier `git diff --stat` showed one added line for camp-state declarations.
- Camp logic is around lines 258–263: `showCampNoise()`, `resolveCampNoise()`, `findCampResources()`, `updateCamp()`, and `toggleCamp()`.
- Driving distance advances in `tick()` around line 337; camp threat must not trigger or alter `showRaid()`.
- An attempted edit failed with `ValueError: substring not found`; no camp behavior changes were made by that script.

## Objective
- Overhaul the survival game in `index.html` while preserving its established layout and gameplay. Finish camp-system balancing and validate the changes.

## Requirements
- Preserve layout, resource/action placement, journey and road-log placement, Van Rig position, resource tiers, repair supplies, part rarity colors, and crew-stress behavior.
- Keep Hull visible in the market; crew skills have two charges per run, camping does not restore charges, and each crew member can recharge once per market for 10 Scrap.
- Keep full skill descriptions on crew cards and concise labels on event skill choices.
- Standard roadside events should have 3–4 contextual choices; avoid generic Ammo trades and universal skill bypasses.
- Use high-cost Ammo trades only in a rare standalone roadside encounter; show skill bypasses only when a trait logically fits.
- Event helper text and numeric keyboard controls should reflect available choices; choices past ten use letter shortcuts.
- Unify applicable crew-trait roadside options so a trait does not appear as both a free-action and a charge-consuming option on one card.
- Part/tire rarity by odometer: Rusted common before 200 miles, then phases out; Worn uncommon before 200, common after; Normal rare before 200, uncommon after 200, common after 300; Pristine very rare before 200, rare after 200, uncommon after 350.
- Balance part tiers from Pristine through Rusted, with tier-appropriate bonuses and drawbacks.
- Minor roadside salvage should occur roughly every 25–40 miles between major events, with a living crew member’s discovery line and Scrap, Fuel, or rare Ammo.
- Ammo broker exact trades: 25 Rations for +1 Ammo (MV +10 stress, ET +10, JP +5); 30 Fuel for +1 Ammo (MV +15, ET +5, JP -5); 30 Scrap for +1 Ammo (MV -5, ET -5, JP -5); refusal has no resource or stress change.
- Add spacing or a separator before the `INSUFFICIENT RESOURCES` warning in event choices.
- Camp state: `campThreat`, `campExhaustion`, and `milesSinceCampReset`; camp actions increase threat/exhaustion, which persist when leaving camp and reset only after driving 50 miles.
- Camp threat tiers: QUIET (actions 1–2), UNSETTLED (3–4), EXPOSED (5–6), COMPROMISED (7+), with tier-appropriate warnings and escalating disturbances, resource costs, and possible Hull/Vitals damage.
- Camp events must never trigger motorcycle raid combat or automatically consume Blaster Ammo.
- Camp Scrap yields should target ~10–25 for short stays, ~30–50 moderate, ~60–90 gross extended stays, with heavy exhaustion-based diminishing returns; retain small Ration/Fuel finds.
- Add “Night Watch / Headlights on the Ridge” choices: wait (-Rations, +Stress), barricade (-Scrap), flee (-Fuel, ends camp), Paranoid concealment (-4 Scrap and reduces Paranoid stress), Sharpshooter watch (1 charge, no material cost).

## Decisions
- Roadside skill choices are event-specific; Sharpshooter applies only to hostile hazards, while Tinkerer bypasses Scrap Storm.
- Skill bypass consumes one charge and clears pending crew-event effects.
- Ammo trader is a standalone encounter selected at 7% chance, without a random crew update.
- Market recharge allowance is tracked per crew member per market stop.
- Part odds use distance-based weight bands with interpolation at 200, 300, and 350 miles; tier stats and drawbacks scale separately.
- Minor salvage awards use the existing Scrap multiplier and respect Fuel’s 100-unit cap.
- Broker stress is applied per member by initials; generic disposition-based stress does not additionally apply to broker choices.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing `index.html` has prior updates for market, crew skills, roadside events, broker encounter, part-tier generation, minor salvage, and camp-state declarations.
- Initial camp state declarations were added: `campThreat`, `campExhaustion`, `milesSinceCampReset`, `campActions`, and `campResetMiles`.

### Active
- Resume camp-system implementation and validation from the actual current contents of `index.html`.

### Blocked
- Camp function edits were not applied: line-based matching reported no matches for `showCampNoise`, `resolveCampNoise`, and `findCampResources`; the final script reported `replaced show/resolve: 0`.
- Syntax validation did not run successfully; `node --check` on the process-substitution path failed with `ENOENT`.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current `index.html` around camp logic and search for function names without assuming prior formatting or line prefixes.
2. Implement persistent camp threat/exhaustion, Night Watch choices, tiered disturbances, and exhaustion-scaled Scrap yields using the actual current source.
3. Update `tick()` to reset threat/exhaustion only after 50 miles driven.
4. Add spacing or a separator before `INSUFFICIENT RESOURCES`.
5. Run inline JavaScript syntax validation and `git diff --check`; review all changes.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, camp logic, and game behavior; previously modified with uncommitted changes.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Overhaul the survival game in `index.html` while preserving its established layout and gameplay. Complete and validate the camp-system balance changes.

## Requirements
- Preserve layout, resource/action placement, journey and road-log placement, Van Rig position, resource tiers, repair supplies, part rarity colors, and crew-stress behavior.
- Keep Hull visible in the market; crew skills have two charges per run, camping does not restore charges, and each crew member can recharge once per market for 10 Scrap.
- Keep full skill descriptions on crew cards and concise labels on event skill choices.
- Standard roadside events should have 3–4 contextual choices; avoid generic Ammo trades and universal skill bypasses.
- Use high-cost Ammo trades only in a rare standalone roadside encounter; show skill bypasses only when a trait logically fits.
- Event helper text and numeric keyboard controls should reflect available choices; choices past ten use letter shortcuts.
- Unify applicable crew-trait roadside options so a trait does not appear as both a free-action and a charge-consuming option on one card.
- Part/tire rarity by odometer: Rusted common before 200 miles, then phases out; Worn uncommon before 200, common after; Normal rare before 200, uncommon after 200, common after 300; Pristine very rare before 200, rare after 200, uncommon after 350.
- Balance part tiers from Pristine through Rusted, with tier-appropriate bonuses and drawbacks.
- Minor roadside salvage should occur roughly every 25–40 miles between major events, with a living crew member’s discovery line and Scrap, Fuel, or rare Ammo.
- Ammo broker exact trades: 25 Rations for +1 Ammo (MV +10 stress, ET +10, JP +5); 30 Fuel for +1 Ammo (MV +15, ET +5, JP -5); 30 Scrap for +1 Ammo (MV -5, ET -5, JP -5); refusal has no resource or stress change.
- Add spacing or a separator before the `INSUFFICIENT RESOURCES` warning in event choices.
- Camp state: `campThreat`, `campExhaustion`, and `milesSinceCampReset`; camp scavenging actions increase threat/exhaustion, which persist when leaving camp and reset only after driving 50 miles.
- Camp threat tiers: QUIET (actions 1–2), UNSETTLED (3–4), EXPOSED (5–6), COMPROMISED (7+), with tier-appropriate warnings and escalating disturbances, resource costs, and possible Hull/Vitals damage.
- Camp events must never trigger motorcycle raid combat or automatically consume Blaster Ammo.
- Camp Scrap yields should target ~10–25 for short stays, ~30–50 moderate, ~60–90 gross extended stays, with heavy exhaustion-based diminishing returns; retain small Ration/Fuel finds.
- Add “Night Watch / Headlights on the Ridge” choices: wait (-Rations, +Stress), barricade (-Scrap), flee (-Fuel, ends camp), Paranoid concealment (-4 Scrap and reduces Paranoid stress), Sharpshooter watch (1 charge, no material cost).

## Decisions
- Roadside skill choices are event-specific; Sharpshooter applies only to hostile hazards, while Tinkerer bypasses Scrap Storm.
- Skill bypass consumes one charge and clears pending crew-event effects.
- Ammo trader is a standalone encounter selected at 7% chance, without a random crew update.
- Market recharge allowance is tracked per crew member per market stop.
- Part odds use distance-based weight bands with interpolation at 200, 300, and 350 miles; tier stats and drawbacks scale separately.
- Minor salvage awards use the existing Scrap multiplier and respect Fuel’s 100-unit cap.
- Broker stress is applied per member by initials; generic disposition-based stress does not additionally apply to broker choices.
- Sharpshooter’s Night Watch skill choice does not increase camp threat or trigger threat-tier damage.
- If no Night Watch option is affordable, add a no-cost “Abandon camp and endure the night” choice that ends camp.

## Work State
### Completed
- Prior updates to `index.html` cover market, crew skills, roadside events, broker encounter, part-tier generation, minor salvage, and camp behavior.
- Camp threat warnings, Night Watch choices, threat-scaled consequences, persistent threat/exhaustion, exhaustion-scaled Scrap finds, and 50-mile driving reset are implemented.
- Updated event-choice resource warnings with a separator and changed helper text to list affordable choices; Night Watch helper likewise lists affordable keys.
- Added a no-cost Night Watch fallback when all other options are unaffordable.
- Inline JavaScript syntax check and `git diff --check` passed before the latest edits.

### Active
- Review camp integration and balance, including latest changes to Night Watch skill effects and the no-affordable-choice fallback.
- Re-run syntax and whitespace checks after latest edits; inspect the full diff and validate runtime behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect camp choice rendering and `resolveCampNoise` to verify the new fallback and Sharpshooter no-threat behavior.
2. Re-run inline JavaScript syntax and `git diff --check`.
3. Review the full `index.html` diff for integration or balance issues.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, roadside systems, and camp behavior.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Camp rewrite was applied by line number after earlier name-based matching failed; inspect current code before further edits.
